Evolution's search process generates reusable biological programs

A meta-analysis, a formal framework, and an operational roadmap for closing the gap between evolutionary search and biological state-transition modeling.
Six-stage analysis · 524 on-target papers · OpenAlex 2015–2024 · review draft

Executive summary

  1. The field splits into learning evolution's outputs vs its process; growth concentrates in outputs.
  2. Reorganized by capability, the embedding pass flipped the reading: the three lowest-confidence capabilities hold the top-3 bridge-opportunity scores (regulatory control ranks #1).
  3. The apparent blind spot is a vocabulary artifact: the harness is modeled to precision in a systems-biology literature overlapping evolution's by 2%.
  4. The two literatures are complementary by module — a closed loop wiring them is the operational path.
  5. Beneath citations they share a computational grammar: 0.71 computation / 0.26 language / 0.0002 citation similarity.
  6. A connectivity matrix localizes the first move: genomic-FM/fitness paradigms × the transitions-attractors harness cluster.

"Evolution is a search process whose outputs are reusable programs — and modern AI is learning to read and rerun them."

The analytical arc

Stage 1

The landscape: two families, one phrase

  • The field splits into learning evolution's outputs (protein/genomic FMs, generative design) vs its process (phylogenetics, forecasting, evo-computation).
  • Growth concentrates in the outputs family: generative design 11×, protein LMs 8× vs pre-2020.
  • 1,766 works → 458 on-target, 10 themed OpenAlex queries, 2015–2024.
Stage 2

The capability reframe — before & after the embedding pass

  • Before (iteration 2, left): capabilities rated inside the evolution-ML literature — regulatory control & predictable adaptation score lowest confidence, looking like the weak link.
  • After (embedding pass, right): a third lens over 524 papers spanning both pillars — shared computation, shared language, vs citation overlap — scores connectivity to the harness literature.
  • The flip is the finding: the three lowest-confidence rows hold the top-3 bridge-opportunity scores — regulatory control ranks #1 (0.71). Their evidence isn't absent — it's un-cited next door.
Stage 3

The generative stack

  • Causal ordering: Pressure → Harness → State Transitions → Programs → Networks → Capability.
  • The middle is modeled with confidence; the generative roots barely at all.
  • State Transitions has high adjacent activity (n≈144) but low modeling depth.
Stage 4

The harness is modeled next door

  • Capability as state function C = f(State, Environment, History, Time); harness as operator H: (state, signal) → state′.
  • State-transition vocabulary surfaces 120 harness-modeling papers the evolution queries never retrieved.
  • The two literatures overlap by only 2% — the blind spot is disconnection, not unmodelability.
Stage 5

The connectivity paradigm & auto-research loop

  • Seven closed-loop modules split almost perfectly by literature — each side owns what the other lacks.
  • The Harness operator is the largest asymmetry (+41 to systems-biology, the exact layer evolution-ML lacks).
  • The loop closes only if every module is wired across both literatures through a shared (state, program) interface.
Stage 6

Reading between the lines: deep connectivity

  • Mapping each paper onto a six-role computational grammar: 7.7% of cross-pillar pairs run near-identical computation.
  • 97.3% of those share zero citations. Fitness landscape ≈ epigenetic landscape — same object, discovered independently.
  • A third semantic-embedding view confirms it: similarity 0.71 computation / 0.26 language / 0.0002 citation (computation & language uncorrelated).
Connectivity matrix

Targeting layer: where to wire first

  • By paradigm: hidden bridges hottest for genomic-FM & fitness paradigms meeting the harness's transitions/attractors & isogenic-variability clusters (0.77–0.79).
  • By role: STATE and OBJECTIVE are the load-bearing shared isomorphism; evolution-ML brings SEARCH, systems-harness brings TRANSITION/REPRESENTATION/FEEDBACK.
  • By capability: the primitive–citation gap is wide and uniform — the disconnect is structural, not local.
  • All three cuts agree on one target: connect a genomic-FM or fitness paradigm to the transitions/attractors harness cluster first.

The roadmap

Four phases from translation to closed loop

Phase 0
State the translation (0–3 mo)
Validate one of 96 pre-identified seed bridges into a worked example; target the genomic-FM/fitness × transitions-attractors cell. Huang, Álvarez-Buylla, Pagnani.
Phase 1
Formalize the harness operator (0–6 mo)
Learn H on a data-rich system (cell-fate reprogramming). Deliverable: a perturbation-validated transition operator. Watson, Pe'er, Nie/Mani.
Phase 2
Make pressure & harness reusable (6–18 mo)
Turn both from bespoke fits into transferable foundation-model modules. Feist/Jensen.
Phase 3
Close the EA↔biology correspondence (18–36 mo)
An evolutionary algorithm whose fitness eval is the learned harness; test whether it rediscovers the programs evolution actually found.
Method & honesty: classification is deterministic keyword logic (noisy per-paper, reliable in aggregate); epistemic-ladder scores are expert priors, not measurements; the six-role grammar is hand-built and interpretable; trend claims capped at 2024. Measured quantities and judgment quantities are labeled as such throughout the component reports.
